messages:
maria: Heads up — Canary (routes v2) rolled at ~1759 and we're seeing sparklines lag on /dashboard. LCP/longtask spike in EU-1 telemetry.

samir: Saw that — is this the new prefetch ordering change from the chunk-split PR? @kai any idea?

kai: yep, PR #4234 changed splitpoint heuristics and adjusted preload list order to prefer shared-chunk. I ran local perf and it looked ok. What do telemetry traces show?

maria: Telemetry summary: main-thread longtasks +120ms median for sparkline paint, bundle for metrics-pane +14kb. Biggest signal is repeated fetches to chunk endpoints — kv-prefetch miss rate jumped.

eva: Repeated fetches how often? got an example log snippet?

maria: Logs:
```
fetch /_assets/chunk-2.js 304
fetch /_assets/chunk-2.js 200
fetch /api/prefetch?key=tile-123 MISS
fetch /api/prefetch?key=tile-123 MISS
```
Seems the ordering change causes prefetch to fire before the kvcache on the chosen pod is warmed, so we end up thrashing MISS -> fetch -> MISS.

samir: That matches the route-affinity tweak — we started rotating requests more aggressively to spread load and that can put requests on pods without warmed caches. Prefetch assumes locality.

kai: Ack. Two paths: 1) revert routing weight change for the canary (fast, lowest risk), or 2) patch prefetch to respect a X-KV-AFFINITY header and delay/serialize when affinity isn't present (safer long-term). Revert is easier short-term.

maria: Can we ship a tiny prefetch guard quickly? If prefetch checks X-KV-AFFINITY and delays a couple hundred ms when unset, it might avoid duplicate fetches. But patch + deploy might take longer than a rollback.

lucas: ops-bot can run a rollback if we decide. ops-bot: run rollback for routes/v2-canary?

evab: small telemetry suggestion — sampling is thin for this flow. Can we bump debug sampler for the canary to capture a few more traces while we investigate?

samir: +1. I'll open a 1-line PR to increment sampling for route=routes/v2-canary and to emit kvcache-hit headers in console logs for easier correlation.

kai: After rollback we should run an experiment: keep the routing change but force prefetch to consult the affinity header — see if locality hints fix it without losing the routing distribution gains.

maria: Agreed. For now let's rollback and monitor. I'll watch the dashboard and post numbers here. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: rollback initiated for routes/v2-canary at 1759098230 — reason: production sparkline lag spike.

ops-bot: rollback completed for routes/v2-canary at 1759098285 — status: success.

maria: Confirmed — dashboard back to baseline. Miss rate down to normal, median sparkline paint returned to pre-rollout numbers. Closing thread. Follow-ups: samir -> sampling & logs PR; kai -> prefetch affinity patch proposal.
